gloss: The chemical element (symbol Xe) with an atomic number of 54. It is a colorless, odorless, unreactive noble gas, used notably in camera flash technology.
One who hates or fears strangers or foreigners.
One who hates or fears extraterrestrial life.
A fear, antipathy, or hatred of strangers or foreigners.
A fear of aliens.
Exhibiting or characterised by xenophobia, a fear or hatred of strangers, foreigners, or extraterrestrial life.

A condition due to a deficiency of vitamin A where the conjunctiva and cornea become dry. The condition starts with conjunctival xerosis and night blindness and progresses to corneal xerosis and, later, a severe condition called keratomalacia.
Very dry, lacking humidity and water.
Adapted to live in a very dry habitat.
Having to do with foreigners.
Relating to strangers or strangeness.
From a foreign place.
From a donor of another species.
The transplantation of biological or organic matter from a given species into a different one, especially when this matter has been altered (such as by genetic engineering)
A small two-masted, and later three-masted, Mediterranean transport ship with an overhanging bow and stern.
A Greek given name.
The pre-Socratic philosopher Xenophanes of Colophon; by extension or reference, any profound or transformative religious thinker.
An attraction to or love of foreign people, manners or culture.
Love (especially sexual love) between humans and extraterrestrials.
A photocopying process in which a negative image formed on an electrically charged plate is transferred as a positive to paper and thermally fixed.
The killing of a stranger or foreigner.
The genocide of an entire alien species.
The intentional killing of an entire foreign (plant or animal) species.
Xerxes I, a Persian king of the Achaemenid dynasty who reigned 485-465 BC.
Xerxes II, a Persian king who ruled for 45 days in 424 BC before being assassinated.
A male given name from Old Persian mainly applied to historical and fictional characters.
A strange form, an alien creature.
An allotriomorph.
Hospitable, especially to visiting strangers or foreigners.
Of the relation between a host and guest; friendly.
A xerox; a photocopy.
something exactly the same as something else
Knowledge of a language one has never learned.
Glossolalia.
Any plant suited for life in a habitat where water is scarce, such as in a desert or chaparral. Such plants may be succulent, have small or reduced leaves, or spines.
A desert plant
Any piece of rock having a different origin to that of the igneous rock in which it is found.
Of, relating to, or characteristic of the xerophytes, especially having the ability to store water in leaves and stems.
Of or pertaining to xerophthalmia.
The speculative biology of extraterrestrial life forms.
The biology of life forms with nonstandard biochemistry or codes, including synthetic life and mirror life.
Study of a language originating from alien species.
The practice of expelling foreigners in Doric Crete and Lacedaemonia.
Any mammal of the superorder Xenarthra, of the Americas; an anteater, armadillo or sloth.
dry; dryness

Political influence achieved by copying and distributing leaflets and similar material.

Someone whose field of study is xenology.
The oxyanion of xenon XeO₄²⁻.
A non-binary gender that is defined not in relation to male or female but by characteristics connected to a thing or concept.
The condition of being xenoparous.
